questions.q: What does a RACI matrix do?
options: Assigns Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed roles to each governance activity
Tracks the budget for the governance program
Measures data quality scores automatically
Replaces the need for a program charter
questions.explain: RACI is a role-clarity tool mapping who does what, who owns it, who's consulted, and who's informed for each activity.

questions.q: In a correctly built RACI matrix, how many people should be marked Accountable for a given activity?
options: Zero — accountability should be implicit
As many as possible, for full collaboration
Exactly one
Exactly the same number as Responsible
questions.explain: The lesson's core discipline: every row needs exactly one Accountable, never zero and never more than one.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say "everyone's a little responsible" is actually a failure mode?
options: It means nobody is actually accountable, and the issue has nowhere specific to land
It violates a legal requirement in every jurisdiction
It is only a problem in very large organizations
It means too many people are doing redundant work
questions.explain: Diffusing accountability across everyone is functionally the same as assigning it to no one.

questions.q: In the lesson's worked RACI example, who is Accountable for drafting a new data policy?
options: The committee
The sponsor
The data owner
The steward
questions.explain: In the example, the owner is Accountable (A) while the steward is Responsible (R) for doing the actual drafting work.

questions.q: Which of these is part of the lesson's practical onboarding sequence for a new governance role?
options: Skipping any written role description to save time
A shadow period with the previous role holder before taking on issues solo
Granting system access only after a full year in the role
Keeping the new role assignment unannounced to avoid overwhelming others
questions.explain: The onboarding sequence includes a written role description, context, tools/access, a shadow period, and a formal announcement — not skipping steps or staying unannounced.
